answer: To limit Sybil farming, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable stake before it can claim rewards. A jetty operator might release payment only after a raven agent completes a verifiable task, with disputes settled through a bridge contract that can slash the stake for fraud. Creating more identities then requires more capital, while successful attacks risk losing it; the cost rises with each Sybil rather than vanishing behind cheap accounts.
